items.title: The rational representation ring $R_{\mathbb Q}(G)$ and rational-valued class functions
The cyclic induction subgroup of the character ring
The cyclic induction subgroup is an ideal of the character ring
items.strategy: Apply the published projection formula to each summand induced from a cyclic subgroup. Multiplication by any class in $R(G)$ stays inside the sum of cyclic induction images, and additivity gives the subgroup property.

items.title: The generator-indicator class function of a cyclic group is obtained by Möbius inversion
items.strategy: For a cyclic group $C$, apply the classical divisor-form Möbius inversion directly to the subgroup-sum function $D \mapsto |D|\,1_D$ to recover the generator-indicator function. Then evaluate $\operatorname{Ind}_D^C 1_D$ by Frobenius' formula in the abelian case to identify the terms with subgroup indicators.

items.title: A positive integer multiple of the trivial character is an integral combination of cyclic permutation characters
items.strategy: Use the generator-indicator class functions from item 4 on each cyclic subgroup and induce them to $G$. Evaluating at $g \in G$, exactly the subgroup generated by a conjugate of $g$ contributes, so the sum is the constant class function $|G|$; then expand each generator-indicator as an integral combination of inductions of trivial characters from cyclic subgroups.

items.title: Artin induction for rational characters
items.strategy: Work in the page convention of item 1: a rational character means a character in $R_{\mathbb Q}(G)$. Item 3 makes the cyclic induction subgroup an ideal, item 5 puts $|G|\,1_G$ inside it, and multiplying by an arbitrary rational character yields $|G|x$ in that subgroup; dividing in $\mathbb Q \otimes R(G)$ gives the claimed rational linear combination.

items.title: Cyclic fixed-space dimensions detect rational virtual characters
items.strategy: For a rational virtual character, the pairings against $\operatorname{Ind}_C^G 1_C$ are the fixed-space dimensions on cyclic subgroups by Frobenius reciprocity and averaging. If all those numbers vanish, Artin induction forces the character itself to vanish, so the fixed-space map is injective.

items.title: The rank of $R_{\mathbb Q}(G)$ is the number of conjugacy classes of cyclic subgroups
items.strategy: Item 7 bounds the rank by the number of cyclic conjugacy classes via the fixed-space detection map. For the reverse inequality, the rational permutation characters $\mathbb Q[G/C]$ for cyclic subgroups $C$ are linearly independent when evaluated at generators of maximal cyclic subgroups.

items.title: Cyclic restrictions force a bounded denominator in the rational representation ring
items.strategy: Multiply the Artin relation by x, apply the projection formula termwise, and use that every cyclic restriction already lies in R(C) to place each induced summand in R(G). The resulting identity gives the controlled denominator |G|x in R(G).

title: Artin Induction and Rational Characters — Examples

items.title: Artin induction is tautological for a cyclic group
items.strategy: When $G$ itself is cyclic, the Artin relation uses $G$ as the maximal cyclic subgroup and collapses to the identity summand. Check the trivial-group case $n=1$ explicitly so the degenerate boundary is not hidden.

items.title: The $A_5$ permutation relation already needs a denominator
items.strategy: Use the cyclic subgroups of orders $1$, $2$, $3$, and $5$ in $A_5$ and the source's explicit Artin relation to verify $[G/C_5]+[G/C_3]+[G/C_2]-[G/C_1]=2\,1_G$. Dividing by $2$ displays the unavoidable denominator in the trivial-character expansion.

items.title: The cyclic fixed-space data recovers an $S_3$ rational character
items.strategy: For the cyclic subgroups $1$, $C_2$, and $A_3$ in $S_3$, compute the fixed-space dimensions of the trivial, sign, and degree-two characters. The resulting three-by-three table is invertible, so the rational virtual character is recovered from those dimensions.

items.title: A rational-valued irreducible character need not come from a $\mathbb Q$-representation
items.strategy: The faithful degree-two character of $Q_8$ has values $(2,-2,0,0,0)$, so it is rational-valued. But the source's Schur-index computation shows that no $\mathbb Q$-representation affords it; on the later RG-3 page this same obstruction is packaged as Schur index $2$ over $\mathbb Q$.
